question: What are the moisture requirements for Grade 1 cloves?
answer: Grade 1 cloves must have a maximum moisture content of 14%. They should be well-dried and pass a snap/brittleness test. Cloves with moisture above 14% will be downgraded by ZSTC.

question: What is the maximum percentage of Mpeta allowed in Grade 1 cloves?
answer: Grade 1 cloves must not contain more than 3% Mpeta (Khoker cloves). If Mpeta exceeds 3% but stays below 7%, the batch falls to Grade 2. Above 7% to 20% is Grade 3. Above 20% Mpeta is classified as Grade 4 (Mpeta grade).

question: What color should Grade 1 cloves be?
answer: Grade 1 cloves must have an attractive saffron or golden color. This color comes from well-matured, properly harvested, and correctly dried cloves. Blackish, faded, or pale brown color indicates Grade 2, Grade 3, or Mpeta (Grade 4).

question: What is Mpeta and why does it matter for my income?
answer: Mpeta (also called Khoker internationally) refers to poorly dried or fermented cloves that are pale brown and soft rather than crisp and golden. ZSTC buys Mpeta at TZS 7,000/kg — 53.3% less than Grade 1 (TZS 15,000/kg). Mpeta is caused by delayed drying, rainy-season drying, or rushing the drying process. Minimizing Mpeta in your batch is the single biggest way to protect your income.

question: What is the ZSTC buying price for each grade of cloves?
answer: The official ZSTC 2023 buying prices are: Grade 1 — TZS 15,000 per kg; Grade 2 — TZS 13,500 per kg (10% less than Grade 1); Grade 3 — TZS 12,500 per kg (16.7% less); Grade 4 (Mpeta) — TZS 7,000 per kg (53.3% less than Grade 1). Accurate drying and handling to achieve Grade 1 gives you the maximum return.

question: How much foreign matter is allowed in cloves?
answer: All grades (Grade 1, 2, and 3) allow a maximum of 5% foreign matter. Foreign matter includes stems (matende), seeds, leaves, and other debris. Always winnow your cloves after drying to remove dust and foreign material before selling to ZSTC.

question: What is the difference between Grade 2 and Grade 3 cloves?
answer: Grade 2 cloves have a slightly blackish or faded color (not as attractive as Grade 1 golden) and allow up to 7% Mpeta. Grade 3 cloves have significantly more faded color, must pass a brittleness/snap test, allow up to 20% Mpeta, and typically contain many headless cloves. Grade 2 fetches TZS 13,500/kg versus TZS 12,500/kg for Grade 3.

question: How does ZSTC grade cloves when buying from farmers?
answer: ZSTC uses a bulk rule-based approach when buying from farmers — they assess the batch as a whole, not individual cloves. They check the overall color, snap/brittleness, moisture level, proportion of Mpeta (Khoker), and percentage of foreign matter in the batch to assign it to Grade 1, 2, 3, or 4.

question: Mpeta ni nini na inathiri vipi bei ya karafuu zangu?
answer: Mpeta (inaitwa pia Khoker kimataifa) ni karafuu ambazo hazikukaushwa vizuri au zilioza. Mpeta ni rangi ya kahawia hafifu na laini badala ya kuwa ngumu. ZSTC inanunua Mpeta kwa TZS 7,000/kg — asilimia 53.3 chini ya daraja la kwanza (TZS 15,000/kg). Mpeta husababishwa na kukawia kukaushwa, kukaushwa wakati wa mvua, au haraka ya kukausha. Kupunguza Mpeta katika mzigo wako ni njia kubwa zaidi ya kulinda mapato yako.

question: Bei za ZSTC za kununua karafuu ni zipi kwa kila daraja?
answer: Bei rasmi za ZSTC za 2023 ni: Daraja la 1 — TZS 15,000 kwa kg; Daraja la 2 — TZS 13,500 kwa kg (pungufu ya 10% kuliko Daraja la 1); Daraja la 3 — TZS 12,500 kwa kg (pungufu ya 16.7%); Daraja la 4 (Mpeta) — TZS 7,000 kwa kg (pungufu ya 53.3% kuliko Daraja la 1). Kukausha vizuri na kushughulikia ipasavyo ili kupata Daraja la 1 kunakupa mapato makubwa zaidi.

question: Karafuu ya Daraja la 1 inapaswa kuwa na rangi gani?
answer: Karafuu ya Daraja la 1 lazima iwe na rangi ya dhahabu au zafarani (saffron/golden). Rangi hii inatoka kwa karafuu iliyokomaa vizuri na kukauswa ipasavyo. Rangi nyeusi kidogo au iliyofifia ni Daraja la 2. Rangi iliyofifia zaidi ni Daraja la 3. Rangi ya kahawia hafifu (pale brown) ni Mpeta/Daraja la 4.

question: Ni asilimia ngapi ya Mpeta inaruhusiwa kwa kila daraja la karafuu?
answer: Daraja la 1: Mpeta haipaswi kuzidi 3%. Daraja la 2: Mpeta haipaswi kuzidi 7%. Daraja la 3: Mpeta haipaswi kuzidi 20%. Daraja la 4 (Mpeta): Inajumuisha Mpeta zaidi ya 20%. Kuhakikisha asilimia ndogo ya Mpeta katika mzigo wako ni muhimu sana kupata bei nzuri kutoka ZSTC.

question: What is the best time to plant cloves in Zanzibar?
answer: The best time to plant cloves is at the onset of the South-West monsoon (June to July). In low-lying areas, plant towards the end of the monsoon season. This timing ensures adequate moisture for establishment without waterlogging.

question: What spacing should I use when planting clove trees?
answer: Plant clove trees 6 to 7 meters apart. Dig planting pits of 75 cm × 75 cm × 75 cm. Partially fill each pit with cattle manure, compost, or green leaf material, then cover with topsoil before planting. If growing cloves as an intercrop with coconut, coffee, or areca nut, base the spacing on the main crop.

question: How do I prepare a nursery for clove seedlings?
answer: Prepare nursery beds as a loose soil-sand mixture, 15–20 cm high and 1 m wide. Spread a 5–8 cm sand layer on top, then sow seeds 2 cm apart. Provide partial shade from direct sunlight. Alternatively, fill 30×15 cm polybags with a 3:3:1 mix of sand, soil, and decomposed organic matter (cow dung). Seeds germinate in 10–15 days. Transplant seedlings from nursery beds to polybags once germinated.

question: How long before a clove tree starts producing?
answer: Clove trees begin flowering from the 4th year under good soil conditions and management. The first commercial harvest is typically at 6–8 years. However, the full bearing stage — peak production — is only reached after 15 years. A 15+ year tree can yield 100–130 kg of dried cloves per year.

question: What fertilizers should I apply to my clove trees?
answer: For young trees (annual application in May–June): Apply 50–60 kg of compost/manure plus bone meal or fish meal. For inorganic fertilizer: 20g N (430g urea), 18g P2O5 (110g superphosphate), and 50g K2O (80g Muriate of Potash) per tree. For mature trees (15+ years): Increase to 300g N, 250g P2O5, and 750g K2O per year, split into two equal doses (May–June and September–October). Apply in shallow trenches 1 to 1.5 meters from the base of the tree, and mulch the basin.

question: When is the right time to harvest cloves?
answer: Harvest clove buds when they change from olive green to yellow-pink, before the petals open. Buds at the correct stage are less than 2 cm long. Once the flower opens, the clove loses its value as a spice. Harvesting too early or too late reduces quality and grade. In Zanzibar, harvesting seasons are approximately April–May and August–October.

question: How do I harvest cloves without damaging the tree?
answer: Use step ladders to reach upper branches. Hand-pick clusters of buds carefully. Do NOT break or remove branches — this permanently reduces the yield of future crops. Detach buds from stalks by holding a cluster in one hand and gently twisting. The workspace and pickers' hands must be clean to avoid contaminating the cloves.

question: Wakati gani bora wa kupanda mkarafuu Zanzibar?
answer: Wakati bora wa kupanda mkarafuu ni mwanzo wa mvua za Kusini Magharibi (Juni hadi Julai). Katika maeneo ya chini, panda mwisho wa mvua. Wakati huu unahakikisha unyevu wa kutosha bila mafuriko. Chimba mashimo ya 75 cm × 75 cm × 75 cm yenye nafasi ya mita 6 hadi 7 kati ya miti.

question: Karafuu inavunwa lini na vipi?
answer: Vuna machipukizi ya karafuu wakati yanabadilika rangi kutoka kijani (olive green) hadi ya njano-pink, kabla maua hayajafunguka. Machipukizi sahihi yana urefu chini ya sentimita 2. Maua yaliyofunguka hayana thamani kama kiungo. Tumia ngazi ili kufikia matawi ya juu. Usivunje matawi kwa sababu hupunguza mavuno ya mwaka ujao. Vuna kwa mikono miti safi.

question: What is Clove Sudden Death disease?
answer: Clove Sudden Death (Kifo cha Ghafla) is a devastating fungal disease caused by Valsa eugeniae (also called Cytospora eugeniae). It is the most serious disease affecting cloves in Zanzibar and Pemba. Symptoms include: leaf fall, wilting leaves turning rust-colored, root rot, yellowing of the inner stem tissue, and yellow leaves from loss of chlorophyll. The pathogen spreads via rainwater from infected roots to neighboring trees. It causes root rot that prevents water transport, killing the tree. Over 500,000 trees in Unguja North were affected in 2024–2025.

question: How do I control Clove Sudden Death disease?
answer: Spray Copper Oxy Chloride (Cooper Oxy Chloride) every 14 days, especially during heavy rain seasons. Consistent preventive spraying is key — do not wait for visible symptoms, as by then damage has progressed. Ensure good drainage around trees because waterlogging accelerates the disease. Remove and destroy heavily infected trees to prevent spread to healthy trees.

question: What is Clove Leaf Spot and how do I treat it?
answer: Clove Leaf Spot is a fungal disease caused by Colletotrichum or Gloeosporium species. The main symptom is black spots on clove leaves. Infected leaves reduce the tree's overall health and productivity. Treatment: Apply a 50/50 mixture of Prophylactic fungicide and Bordeaux mixture. These products are available at Agrovet shops or from your local agricultural extension officer (Bwana Shamba).

question: What is the Clove Stem Borer and how do I deal with it?
answer: The Clove Stem Borer (Dumuzi/Kipekecha Shuna) is an insect pest that attacks the mature lower stem of the clove tree. It lays eggs, and larvae bore through the outer bark into the core of the stem, weakening and eventually killing the tree. Control measures: (1) Keep the farm clean — remove weeds, grass, and rotting logs that serve as breeding grounds. (2) Spray Fenthion or Cypermethrin insecticides. (3) For active bore holes, apply 2–4 ml of kerosene or paraffin directly into the hole to kill the larva inside.

question: How do I control scale insects on my clove trees?
answer: Scale insects (Mdudu Gamba) live under leaves or on young stems. They suck plant sap, causing leaves to curl, turn yellow, and drop. They also produce black sooty mold that blocks photosynthesis. Control with insecticides containing any of: Dimethoate, Acephate, Bifenthrin, Malathion, Permethrin, Imidacloprid, or Thiamethoxam. Also avoid overcrowding trees, and prune dense canopy areas.

question: Ugonjwa wa Kifo cha Ghafla ni nini na unatibiwa vipi?
answer: Ugonjwa wa Kifo cha Ghafla (Clove Sudden Death) ni ugonjwa wa fangasi unaosababishwa na Valsa eugeniae (pia huitwa Cytospora eugeniae). Dalili ni: majani kupukutika, majani kunyauka na kuwa rangi ya kutu, kuoza kwa mizizi, njano ya ndani ya shina, na majani ya njano. Ugonjwa husambazwa na maji ya mvua kutoka mizizi ya mti ulioathirika. Matibabu: Nyunyuzia kiuatilifu cha COPPER OXY CHLORIDE kila baada ya siku 14, haswa wakati wa mvua nyingi. Usisimame hadi uone dalili — zingatie kinga mapema.

question: Wadudu gamba wanaathirije mti wa mkarafuu na wanatibiwa vipi?
answer: Wadudu gamba (Insects Scale) hukaa chini ya majani au sehemu ya shina lisilokomaa. Hufyonza maji kwenye majani, majani kukunjamana, kubadilika kuwa njano, na kudondoka. Pia wanauzalisha utando mweusi unaoathiri chanikiwiti (chlorophyll). Tumia viuadudu vyenye: Dimethoate, Acephate, Bifenthrin, Malathion, Permethrin, Imidacloprid, au Thiamethoxam. Pia punguza msongamano wa miti na kata matawi yanayotengeneza msitu mzito.

question: How long does it take to dry cloves properly?
answer: Proper sun drying takes 4 to 5 days. Spread buds on clean mats, rake and turn them frequently for even drying. Do not rush the process — cloves dried too fast become dry, brittle, and withered (reducing quality). The color should progress from pale russet to dark brown. Fully dried cloves snap (break) easily. Target moisture content: 8–10% for storage; ZSTC accepts up to 14% moisture.

question: What happens if my cloves get wet during drying?
answer: If cloves get wet or are dried during rain, they ferment and turn into Mpeta (Khoker) — Grade 4, which ZSTC buys at only TZS 7,000/kg (53.3% below Grade 1 price). During rainy season, always use a mechanical dryer (such as a tray dryer) rather than sun drying. Never leave cloves exposed to rain or high humidity before they are fully dried.

question: How do I store cloves after drying to maintain quality?
answer: Store dried cloves in sealed, moisture-proof containers away from direct sunlight. The storage room must be clean, dry, cool, and pest-free. Install mosquito netting on windows. Do NOT store cloves near strong-smelling items like detergents, paints, or strong foods — these contaminate the clove aroma. Inspect stored cloves regularly. If they absorb moisture, re-dry to 10% moisture before selling.

question: Karafuu inakaushwa kwa muda gani na jinsi gani?
answer: Kukausha kwa jua huchukua siku 4 hadi 5. Sambaza machipukizi kwenye mikeka safi, vipiga na vigeuze mara kwa mara ili vikauke sawasawa. Usifanye haraka — karafuu iliyokaushwa haraka inakuwa kavu sana na inazidishwa kuwa Daraja la 3 au Mpeta. Rangi inapaswa kwenda kutoka kahawia hafifu hadi kahawia giza. Karafuu iliyokauka vizuri huvunjika kwa urahisi (brittle/snap test). Ikiwa ni msimu wa mvua, tumia kikaushio cha mitambo (tray dryer).

question: Je, ninahifadhi karafuu vipi baada ya kukausha?
answer: Hifadhi karafuu iliyokaushwa ndani ya makontena yaliyofungwa vizuri, mbali na jua moja kwa moja. Chumba cha kuhifadhia kiwe safi, kikavu, kipoa, na kisicho na wadudu. Weka nyavu kwenye madirisha kuzuia wadudu. Usihifadhi karibu na vitu vya harufu kali kama sabuni, rangi, au vyakula vikali — vitu hivi vinaharibu harufu ya karafuu. Kagua mara kwa mara. Ikiwa karafuu imenyonya unyevu, ikaushe tena hadi unyevu wa 10% kabla ya kuuza.

question: Who buys cloves from farmers in Zanzibar?
answer: All cloves in Zanzibar must be sold to the ZSTC (Zanzibar State Trading Corporation), which is the government-owned entity that has a legal monopsony on clove purchases. ZSTC buys from farmers at officially set prices by grade, then exports the cloves internationally. Farmers cannot legally sell directly to private buyers or export on their own.

question: What caused the big drop in Zanzibar clove exports in 2025?
answer: The 2024–2025 export collapse had several causes: (1) Sudden Death disease destroyed over 500,000 trees in Unguja North; (2) Erratic rainfall (Indian Ocean Dipole climate events) caused flower drop and poor drying conditions, producing low-grade and Mpeta cloves; (3) The tree stock is aging, with many trees from the 1960s–70s past peak productivity; (4) Some cloves were smuggled to Kenya through unofficial channels, bypassing ZSTC. Export volume fell from 3,900 to 1,200 tonnes, and value fell from $28.8 million to $6.3 million.

question: Ni nani anayenunua karafuu kutoka kwa wakulima Zanzibar?
answer: Karafuu zote Zanzibar lazima ziuzwe kwa ZSTC (Zanzibar State Trading Corporation), ambayo ni shirika la serikali lenye haki ya pekee ya kununua karafuu (monopsony). ZSTC inanunua kutoka kwa wakulima kwa bei rasmi kulingana na daraja, kisha inasafirisha nje ya nchi. Wakulima hawawezi kuuza moja kwa moja kwa wanunuzi binafsi kwa mujibu wa sheria.
